title: It's ok. Filter lasts about a month.
text:
It's ok. Filter lasts about a month.. Physically, what I don't like about this pitcher is that the little "handle" they put in the lid so you can lift it off is pointless. The lid snaps in, and the little groove you're supposed to grip to lift it off isn't nearly sufficient. So you end up sticking your finger in the end where the water comes out, which I don't really care about but someone might if they're very concerned about germs.
Secondly, the pitcher really doesn't filter much at a time. Even if you fill it once and then refill it again, the second time the water takes so long to filter that it's just easier to do it one at a time.

I like the way the water tastes when it's filtered. It's not for everyone. It's like how it tastes when you buy bottled water that's been "mineralized for taste", which really confuses me since this supposed to filter out most things. But whatever--I still like the taste of it.

However, I actually bought this not to drink with but to water my plants and fill my humidifier. I have a few sensitive plants that demand distilled water, rain water, or super filtered water like this (living in the desert prevents me from collecting rain water). Since I don't have to water my plants a lot I'll probably keep using it for that.

I was using it to fill my humidifier each night to prevent the "white dust" that can settle around humidifiers and also prevent hard water build up inside it. It was certainly effective, but I had to use so much water just to fill up my humidifier each night that I used up the filter fairly quickly. I filled the pitcher probably 3 times per day for my humidifier, plus add in a few extra fills for watering my plants, and the filter lasted about a month.

After about five weeks of using my humidifier with this pitcher, my humidifier started smelling fishy, which I thought was strange considering I had just cleaned it the week before. I ended up cleaning my humidifier multiple times and refilling it thinking it was my humidifier at fault, but I was wrong. I finally thought to smell the water that was filtered from the pitcher and it was the water that was smelling fishy. So obviously the filter had run its course. I tested with the TDS meter just to see what the filtered water was at, and it read 088.

Considering these filters cost over $12 a piece, I am not going to continue to use the pitcher to fill my humidifier. I'll just deal with the hard water consequences. I will continue to use it for my plants and I'll probably start drinking it since I liked the taste. I'll be interested to see how long a filter last doing that.

5-Stage Filtration: Removes virtually all total dissolved solids (TDS) for the purest tasting water; Total Dissolved Solids are organic and inorganic materials, such as metals, minerals, salts, and ions dissolved in water.
NSF certified and BPA free: The Only Pour Through Filter Certified by NSF to Reduce Lead, Chromium and PFOA/PFOS; All material is BPA free
Including: 12-cup Water Pitcher, 1 ZeroWater 5-Stage Filter with Ion Exchange Technology and a Free TDS Meter
Eco-Friendly: Save up to 300 single-use plastic bottles per filter or up to 1800 bottles a year while enjoying the purest tasting water
description: The 12 Cup 5-stage Water Filtration Pitcher with Ready-Pour™ technology is a great option for a busy household and provides you and your family with easy access to filtered water through the “Quick Fill” spigot. The Ready-Pour™ technology suits your on-the-go lifestyle - you can dispense delicious water while the reservoir is still filtering.
